questions.question: An object placed between F and 2F of a convex lens forms an image _________.

options.text: At infinity, real, inverted and same size
Between F and the lens, virtual, erect, and diminished

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Beyond 2F, real, inverted, and enlarged**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• When an object is placed between the **focal point (F)** and **twice the focal length (2F)** of a convex lens, the image formed is located **beyond 2F**.
 
• The image is **real and inverted**, which means it can be projected on a screen and is flipped upside down relative to the object.
 
• Additionally, the image is **enlarged**, meaning it is larger than the object itself.
 
• This happens due to the **converging nature** of the convex lens, which bends parallel light rays to meet at a point (focus).
 
• This property of convex lenses makes them essential for applications such as magnifying glasses, microscopes, and telescopes.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Convex Lens:**

 
 
• A convex lens is a lens that is thicker at the center than at the edges.
 
• It is also known as a **converging lens** because it bends light rays towards a single focal point.
 
• Convex lenses are used in **optical devices** such as cameras, projectors, and eyeglasses for hypermetropia (farsightedness).
 
 
 
• **Image Formation by Convex Lens:**
 
 
• The position and nature of the image formed by a convex lens depend on the **object's distance** from the lens.
 
• When the object is beyond 2F, the image is formed **between F and 2F**, real, inverted, and diminished.
 
• When the object is at 2F, the image is formed **at 2F**, real, inverted, and the same size.
 
• When the object is between F and 2F, the image is formed **beyond 2F**, real, inverted, and enlarged.
 
• When the object is at F, the image is formed **at infinity**, real, inverted, and highly enlarged.
 
• When the object is between F and the lens, the image is formed **behind the lens**, virtual, erect, and enlarged.
 
 
 
• **Lens Formula:**
 
 
• The lens formula is given by: **(1/f) = (1/v) - (1/u)**, where:
 
• **f**: Focal length of the lens
 
• **v**: Image distance from the lens
 
• **u**: Object distance from the lens
 
• This formula helps determine the image position and magnification for a given object distance.
 
 
 
• **Applications of Convex Lenses:**
 
 
• Used in **magnifying glasses** to enlarge objects for better visibility.
 
• Integral in the design of **microscopes** and **telescopes** for scientific research and exploration.
 
• Used in **projectors** to focus and enlarge images on a screen.
 
• Commonly used in **eyeglasses** to correct farsightedness.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The nature of the image produced by a convex lens depends on the object's location relative to the lens's focal points (F and 2F).
 
• Convex lenses are widely used for **focusing light** in various optical instruments.
 
• Understanding the principles of image formation by lenses is crucial in fields such as **optics**, **physics**, and **engineering**.
 
• The magnification of an image can be calculated using the formula: **Magnification = Image Height / Object Height = v/u**.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is correct?

options.text: Work requires both force and displacement.
The work can be done without displacement.
Work can be done without force.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Work requires both force and displacement.**__.
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**
 

__ 
 
• Work is defined as the product of force applied on an object and the displacement of the object in the direction of the force. The formula is: **W = F × d × cos(θ)**, where **F** is force, **d** is displacement, and **θ** is the angle between the force and displacement. 
 
• For work to be done, **both force and displacement must exist**. If either force or displacement is zero, the work done becomes zero. Hence, the statement "Work requires both force and displacement__" is correct. 
 
• The second statement, "__The work can be done without displacement__", is incorrect because displacement is a necessary condition for work to occur. 
 
• The third statement, "__Work is independent of displacement__", is also incorrect as displacement directly influences the amount of work done. 
 
• The fourth statement, "__Work can be done without force__", is incorrect, as force is a fundamental factor in the calculation of work. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

__ 
 
• **Conditions for Work:** 
 
 
• There must be a force acting on the object. 
 
• The object must undergo displacement. 
 
• The displacement must have a component in the direction of the force applied. 
 
 
 
• **Types of Work:** 
 
 
• **Positive Work:** When the force and displacement are in the same direction, such as lifting an object upward. 
 
• **Negative Work:** When the force and displacement are in opposite directions, such as friction acting against the motion of a sliding object. 
 
• **Zero Work:** When there is no displacement, or the force is perpendicular to the displacement, such as holding an object stationary or circular motion where the force is perpendicular to displacement. 
 
 
 
• **Units of Work:** 
 
 
• The SI unit of work is the **joule (J)**. 1 Joule = 1 Newton × 1 meter (N·m). 
 
• Other units include erg (used in CGS system) and foot-pound (in FPS system). 
 
 
 
• **Applications of Work:** 
 
 
• **Mechanical Systems:** Work is essential in lifting objects, pulling loads, and operating machines. 
 
• **Energy Transfer:** Work is a form of energy transfer, converting potential energy into kinetic energy or vice versa. 
 
• **Power Calculation:** Work is used to calculate power, which is work done per unit time. 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**
 

 
 
• **Work and Energy Relationship:** Work is directly related to energy. The work done on an object changes its energy, following the **Work-Energy Theorem**, which states that the work done by all forces is equal to the change in kinetic energy. 
 
• **Friction and Work:** Friction does negative work as it opposes the direction of motion, dissipating energy as heat. 
 
• **Work in Gravitational Fields:** When an object is lifted against gravity, work is done against the gravitational force, and potential energy is stored. 
 
• **Practical Examples:** Activities like pushing a trolley, lifting a box, or pulling a rope involve work being done.

questions.question: In which of the following simple permanent tissues the cell walls are lignified?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Sclerenchyma**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Sclerenchyma** is a type of simple permanent tissue in plants that provides structural support and mechanical strength.
 
• The cell walls of sclerenchyma are heavily **lignified**, which means they are thickened by the deposition of lignin, making them hard and rigid.
 
• Sclerenchyma cells are usually dead at maturity and lack protoplasm, allowing them to solely function in support.
 
• This tissue can be found in various parts of plants, such as stems, roots, veins of leaves, and hard shells of seeds and fruits.
 
• Sclerenchyma cells are of two types: **fibers** (elongated cells) and **sclereids** (irregularly shaped cells). Both types have lignified walls.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Phloem:**

 
 
• Phloem is a complex permanent tissue involved in the transport of food in plants.
 
• It consists of sieve tubes, companion cells, phloem parenchyma, and phloem fibers.
 
• While phloem fibers are lignified, the rest of the components are not, making the phloem not entirely lignified.
 
 
 
• **Parenchyma:**
 
 
• Parenchyma is a simple permanent tissue composed of living cells with thin, non-lignified cell walls.
 
• It is involved in storage, photosynthesis, and secretion in plants.
 
• Examples include mesophyll cells in leaves and storage tissues in fruits.
 
 
 
• **Collenchyma:**
 
 
• Collenchyma is a simple permanent tissue that provides mechanical support and flexibility to growing plant parts.
 
• Its cells have unevenly thickened walls made of cellulose and pectin, not lignin.
 
• It is found in leaf stalks, stems, and petioles.
 
 
 
• **Lignification:**
 
 
• Lignification is the process of depositing lignin in the cell walls, making them rigid and resistant to decay.
 
• Lignin is a complex organic polymer that is a key structural component of plant cell walls.
 
• This process is essential for the mechanical strength of tissues like sclerenchyma and xylem.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Applications of Sclerenchyma:**

 
 
• Fibers from sclerenchyma are used in making ropes, mats, and textiles (e.g., jute and coir).
 
• Sclereids contribute to the hardness of seed coats, fruit shells, and nuts.
 
 
 
• **Examples of lignified tissues:**
 
 
• Xylem vessels and tracheids, which are involved in water transport, are also lignified.
 
• These tissues, like sclerenchyma, provide structural support to plants.

questions.question: Which of the following is a heterogeneous mixture?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Soil**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Heterogeneous Mixture:** A heterogeneous mixture consists of visibly different substances or phases. These components do not blend completely, and their individual properties remain distinct.
 
• **Soil:** Soil is a prime example of a heterogeneous mixture. It contains various components like sand, clay, silt, organic matter, and other materials that can be seen separately. These components are unevenly distributed, making soil a heterogeneous mixture.
 
• **Air:** Air is a homogeneous mixture as it is a uniform composition of gases like nitrogen, oxygen, carbon dioxide, and others. The gases are evenly distributed throughout (hence, this is not the correct answer).
 
• **Vinegar:** Vinegar is another homogeneous mixture where acetic acid is uniformly dissolved in water (hence, this is not the correct answer).
 
• **Sugar Solution:** A sugar solution is a homogeneous mixture where sugar is uniformly dissolved in water, forming a single phase (hence, this is not the correct answer).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Heterogeneous Mixtures:**

 
 
• Heterogeneous mixtures have non-uniform compositions. The different components can be easily identified.
 
• Examples include soil, trail mix, salads, and oil-water mixtures.
 
• The phases in a heterogeneous mixture might be in solid, liquid, or gaseous forms.
 
 
 
• **Homogeneous Mixtures:**
 
 
• Homogeneous mixtures have a uniform composition throughout, and the individual components cannot be visually distinguished.
 
• Examples include saltwater, air, and vinegar.
 
• Homogeneous mixtures are often referred to as solutions when one substance is dissolved in another.
 
 
 
• **Key Characteristics of Soil:**
 
 
• Soil is composed of minerals, organic matter, air, and water.
 
• It varies in texture, structure, and nutrient content depending on its type and location.
 
• Soil also contains living organisms such as bacteria, fungi, and insects, which contribute to its heterogeneous nature.
 
 
 
• **Applications of Soil:**
 
 
• Soil is essential for agriculture, providing a medium for plant growth and nutrient supply.
 
• It plays a key role in water filtration, acting as a natural filter for rainwater and surface water.
 
• Soil is also used in construction (e.g., clay for bricks) and as a raw material in various industries.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Differences between Homogeneous and Heterogeneous Mixtures:**

 
 
• In homogeneous mixtures, the composition is uniform, whereas in heterogeneous mixtures, it is not.
 
• Homogeneous mixtures are typically in a single phase, while heterogeneous mixtures can have multiple phases.
 
• Examples of homogeneous mixtures include saltwater and air, while examples of heterogeneous mixtures include soil and salad.
 
 
 
• **Real-World Examples of Heterogeneous Mixtures:**
 
 
• **Concrete:** A mixture of cement, sand, gravel, and water.
 
• **Oil and Water:** Two immiscible liquids forming a heterogeneous mixture.
 
• **Granite:** A rock composed of distinct minerals like quartz, feldspar, and mica.

questions.question: Which of the following pairs correctly matches the device with its main use?

options.text: Stethoscope – Directing sound to a large audience

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Megaphone – Listening to heartbeat**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Stethoscope:**

 
 
• The stethoscope is a medical device designed specifically for **listening to internal body sounds**, such as the heartbeat, lung sounds, and intestinal sounds.
 
• It is not used for **directing sound to a large audience**, as stated in option 1, making the statement **incorrect**.
 
 
 
• **Horn:**
 
 
• A horn is typically used for **amplifying sound** or as a signaling device in automobiles or musical instruments.
 
• It cannot measure **blood pressure**, as suggested in option 3, making the statement **incorrect**.
 
 
 
• **Megaphone:**
 
 
• A megaphone is a device used to **amplify sound** and project it over a distance, generally for public speaking or announcements.
 
• It is not used for **listening to a heartbeat**, making option 4 **incorrect**.
 
 
 
• **Correct Pairing:**
 
 
• Among the given options, none correctly matches the device to its primary purpose.
 
• The correct use of these devices must align with their **functional design** and intended purpose.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Stethoscope:**

 
 
• Invented by **René Laennec in 1816**, the stethoscope is widely used in healthcare for auscultation (listening to the internal sounds of the body).
 
• It comprises earpieces, tubing, and a chest piece that detects sound vibrations from the body.
 
• It is essential for diagnosing heart and lung conditions, such as **murmurs, arrhythmias, or respiratory issues**.
 
 
 
• **Horn:**
 
 
• Primarily used in vehicles, horns serve as a warning or communication device.
 
• Musical horns, like those in orchestras, amplify sound to enhance musical performances.
 
• Instruments like the **French horn** are specifically tuned to produce musical notes.
 
 
 
• **Megaphone:**
 
 
• A megaphone amplifies a person’s voice, allowing it to be heard over a large area.
 
• It is commonly used in public gatherings, protests, and emergencies to convey messages clearly.
 
• Modern megaphones often include **electronic amplification** for enhanced output.
 
 
 
• **Blood Pressure Measurement:**
 
 
• Blood pressure is measured using a device called a **sphygmomanometer**, not a horn.
 
• It typically involves an inflatable cuff, a measuring gauge, and a stethoscope for listening to the Korotkoff sounds.
 
• This technique helps diagnose conditions like **hypertension or hypotension**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Amplification Devices:** Megaphones and horns are devices designed for amplifying sound. Their specific applications differ, with megaphones focusing on voice projection and horns serving as warning or musical devices.
 
• **Medical Instruments:** The stethoscope is a specialized tool in medicine, while the sphygmomanometer is essential for blood pressure measurement, often combined with the stethoscope.
 
• **Historical Context:** Many of these devices have evolved over time, such as the stethoscope improving with electronic enhancements for better diagnostic accuracy.
 
• **Specialized Use:** Each device serves a unique purpose, and their functionality is tailored to specific needs, such as medical diagnostics, sound amplification, or signaling.

questions.question: Which of the following reactions correctly represents the synthesis of bleaching powder?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**2**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Bleaching powder (CaOCl₂)** is synthesized by reacting **chlorine gas (Cl₂)** with **slaked lime (Ca(OH)₂).**
 
• The chemical equation for the synthesis is: **2Ca(OH)₂ + 2Cl₂ → Ca(ClO)₂ + CaCl₂ + 2H₂O**. This correctly represents the reaction for bleaching powder synthesis.
 
• In this reaction, **chlorine gas** reacts with slaked lime to form a mixture of calcium oxychloride (**CaOCl₂**) and calcium chloride (**CaCl₂**).
 
• **Bleaching powder** is widely used as a disinfectant and bleaching agent due to its strong oxidizing properties.
 
• This process is carried out on an industrial scale, where chlorine gas is passed over dry slaked lime under controlled conditions to produce **bleaching powder.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Uses of Bleaching Powder:**

 
 
• **Disinfectant:** It is commonly used for disinfecting drinking water to kill harmful pathogens.
 
• **Bleaching agent:** It is used to bleach cotton, linen, and wood pulp in the textile and paper industries.
 
• **Oxidizing agent:** It is employed in chemical industries for various oxidation reactions.
 
• **Sanitation:** Bleaching powder is used in public sanitation for cleaning drains and toilets.
 
 
 
• **Manufacturing Process:**
 
 
• Bleaching powder is manufactured in chambers where chlorine gas is passed over dry slaked lime.
 
• The reaction is carried out under controlled temperature and pressure to ensure efficiency.
 
 
 
• **Chemical Properties:**
 
 
• Bleaching powder is a yellowish-white powder with a strong chlorine smell.
 
• It decomposes in water to release hypochlorous acid, which is responsible for its bleaching and disinfecting properties.
 
 
 
• **Safety Precautions:**
 
 
• Bleaching powder should be stored in airtight containers to prevent its reaction with moisture in the air.
 
• It should be handled with gloves and protective gear due to its corrosive nature.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Common Misconceptions:**

 
 
• Bleaching powder is often confused with sodium hypochlorite, which is a liquid bleach commonly used in households.
 
• While both are used for disinfection, their chemical compositions and applications differ significantly.
 
 
 
• **Historical Context:**
 
 
• Bleaching powder was first introduced in the early 19th century and became widely popular in water treatment and sanitation practices.
 
• Its discovery revolutionized the bleaching and disinfection processes in various industries.
 
 
 
• **Environmental Impact:**
 
 
• Excessive use of bleaching powder can lead to chlorine pollution in water bodies, which is harmful to aquatic life.
 
• Proper disposal and controlled usage are essential to minimize environmental damage.

questions.question: Which of the following substances is inert in nature and remains present in the environment for a long period and damages various components of the ecosystem?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Disposable plastic cups**__.
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**
 

__ 
 
• **Disposable plastic cups** are made of non-biodegradable materials like polystyrene or polypropylene, which take hundreds of years to decompose in the environment. 
 
• These plastics are **inert in nature**, meaning they do not react with environmental factors like sunlight, water, or microorganisms, leading to long-term persistence in ecosystems. 
 
• The accumulation of plastic waste leads to the **pollution of soil, water bodies, and marine ecosystems**, impacting biodiversity and ecological balance. 
 
• Plastics break down into **microplastics**, which are ingested by animals and enter the food chain, posing health risks to humans and wildlife. 
 
• Unlike biodegradable materials such as paper, tea leaves, or clay (kullhads), plastic cups are a major contributor to environmental damage due to their **resistance to natural degradation**. 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**
 

__ 
 
• **Disposable paper cups:** 
 
 
• Made primarily from paperboard and are generally biodegradable. 
 
• They decompose in a short period, especially in compostable conditions, causing minimal environmental harm. 
 
• However, some paper cups are lined with plastic to make them waterproof, complicating their decomposition. 
 
 
 
• **Tea leaves:** 
 
 
• Tea leaves are **organic and fully biodegradable**. 
 
• They decompose quickly in the soil, enriching it with nutrients and improving its fertility. 
 
• Tea leaves do not pose any long-term environmental risks. 
 
 
 
• **Clay kullhads:** 
 
 
• Made from natural clay, these are **eco-friendly and biodegradable**. 
 
• They break down into the soil naturally over time without causing pollution. 
 
• Clay kullhads have been a traditional alternative to disposable plastic and are considered sustainable. 
 
 
 
• **Impact of disposable plastic:** 
 
 
• Globally, it is estimated that **over 300 million tons of plastic waste** are generated annually. 
 
• More than **8 million tons** of plastic enter oceans every year, affecting marine life. 
 
• Plastic pollution has prompted several nations to impose bans or restrictions on single-use plastics. 
 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**
 

 
 
• **Government Initiatives to Reduce Plastic Use:** 
 
 
• In 2019, India pledged to eliminate **single-use plastics** by 2022, although this target remains a challenge. 
 
• Several Indian states like **Maharashtra, Tamil Nadu, and Himachal Pradesh** have introduced bans on plastic carry bags and disposable items. 
 
• Globally, countries like **Canada, EU nations, and Rwanda** have adopted stringent measures to curb plastic pollution. 
 
 
 
• **Alternatives to Plastic:** 
 
 
• Biodegradable materials like paper, jute, and bamboo are being promoted as sustainable options. 
 
• Innovations such as **bioplastics** made from corn starch or sugarcane are gaining popularity. 
 
• Reusable items like stainless steel or glass containers are encouraged to reduce plastic dependency.

questions.question: If a person weighing 600 N stands on two feet whose total contact area is, find the pressure exerted on the sand?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**12,000 Pa**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **pressure** exerted by an object is calculated using the formula: **Pressure = Force / Area**.
 
• The **force** exerted by the person is equal to their **weight**, which is given as **600 N**.
 
• The area of contact of the feet is **0.05 m²** (not explicitly mentioned in the question but derived from the correct answer).
 
• Using the formula: **Pressure = 600 N / 0.05 m² = 12,000 Pa**.
 
• Thus, the **correct pressure** exerted on the sand is **12,000 Pa**.
 
• *Hence, the correct answer is **12,000 Pa**__.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Pressure:**

 
 
• Pressure is defined as the **force exerted per unit area**.
 
• The SI unit of pressure is the **Pascal (Pa)**, where 1 Pa = 1 N/m².
 
• It is a scalar quantity, meaning it has magnitude but no direction.
 
• Examples of pressure in daily life include tire pressure, atmospheric pressure, and pressure applied by sharp objects.
 
 
 
• **Force and Weight:**
 
 
• Force is measured in **Newtons (N)**, and weight is the force due to gravity acting on an object.
 
• Weight is calculated as **W = mg**, where **m** is mass (in kg) and **g** is the acceleration due to gravity (approximately 9.8 m/s²).
 
• In this scenario, the weight of the person is directly given as **600 N**.
 
 
 
• **Area:**
 
 
• Area is the two-dimensional space over which the force is distributed.
 
• In this case, the area is assumed to be the total contact area of the person's feet, which is **0.05 m²**.
 
• Smaller contact areas result in greater pressure for the same force.
 
 
 
• **Applications of Pressure:**
 
 
• Pressure calculations are essential in fields like engineering, meteorology, and medicine.
 
• Examples include the design of hydraulic systems, pressure cookers, and even footwear to evenly distribute weight.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Factors Affecting Pressure:**

 
 
• Pressure increases with an increase in **force** or a decrease in **area**.
 
• For example, a sharp knife cuts better than a blunt one because it exerts more pressure on a smaller area.
 
 
 
• **Units of Pressure:**
 
 
• Common units include **Pascal (Pa)**, **atmosphere (atm)**, and **bar**.
 
• 1 atm = 101,325 Pa, and 1 bar = 100,000 Pa.
 
 
 
• **Practical Implications:**
 
 
• In construction, understanding pressure helps in designing strong foundations for buildings to distribute weight effectively.
 
• In footwear design, proper distribution of pressure ensures comfort and prevents injuries.

questions.question: Which gland in the human body secretes growth hormone?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ptuitary gland**__.
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**
 
__ 
 
• The **pituitary gland**, often referred to as the "master gland," is responsible for secreting the **growth hormone**, also known as **somatotropin**. 
 
• The growth hormone plays a critical role in **stimulating growth, cell reproduction, and cell regeneration** in humans. 
 
• It is secreted by the **anterior lobe of the pituitary gland**, which is located at the base of the brain in a small bony cavity called the **sella turcica**. 
 
• **Growth hormone secretion** is regulated by the hypothalamus through the release of **growth hormone-releasing hormone (GHRH)** and inhibited by **somatostatin**. 
 
• The hormone has significant effects on **bone growth** during childhood and adolescence, as well as on **metabolism** by promoting protein synthesis and the breakdown of fats. 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**
 
__ 
 
• **Pituitary Gland:** 
 
 
• It is a pea-shaped gland located at the base of the brain, connected to the hypothalamus by a stalk called the **infundibulum**. 
 
• The pituitary gland is divided into two main parts: the **anterior pituitary** and the **posterior pituitary**. The anterior pituitary is responsible for releasing growth hormone. 
 
• Other hormones secreted by the pituitary include **prolactin, ACTH (adrenocorticotropic hormone), TSH (thyroid-stimulating hormone), FSH (follicle-stimulating hormone), and LH (luteinizing hormone)**. 
 
 
 
• **Functions of Growth Hormone:** 
 
 
• Stimulates the growth of bones and tissues, especially during childhood and puberty. 
 
• Regulates **metabolism** by increasing protein synthesis, promoting fat breakdown, and maintaining blood glucose levels. 
 
• Plays a role in **repairing tissues** and enhancing muscle growth in adults. 
 
 
 
• **Disorders Related to Growth Hormone:** 
 
 
• **Gigantism:** Caused by excessive secretion of growth hormone during childhood, leading to abnormally tall stature. 
 
• **Acromegaly:** Caused by excessive growth hormone secretion in adults, resulting in the enlargement of bones in the face, hands, and feet. 
 
• **Dwarfism:** Caused by insufficient secretion of growth hormone during childhood, leading to stunted growth. 
 
 
 
• **Other Glands Mentioned in Options:** 
 
 
• **Adrenal Gland:** Located on top of the kidneys, it secretes hormones such as adrenaline, cortisol, and aldosterone, which are involved in stress response and metabolism. 
 
• **Pancreas:** Functions as both an endocrine and exocrine gland. It releases insulin and glucagon, which regulate blood sugar levels. 
 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**
 
 
 
• The secretion of growth hormone is **highest during puberty** and gradually declines with age. 
 
• Growth hormone therapy is used for individuals with **growth hormone deficiency** to promote normal growth and development. 
 
• Growth hormone levels can also be affected by factors such as sleep, exercise, and nutrition. 
 
• The pituitary gland is often referred to as the "master gland" because it controls the functioning of other endocrine glands, such as the thyroid and adrenal glands.

__
 
• The **stigma** is the topmost part of the pistil (female reproductive structure of the flower) where the **pollen grain lands for fertilization**. It plays a crucial role in the reproduction process of flowering plants.
 
• The stigma is often **sticky** or has a specialized surface to effectively trap and hold pollen grains during pollination.
 
• Once the pollen grain adheres to the stigma, it germinates and forms a **pollen tube**, which grows down the style to reach the ovary for fertilization.
 
• The stigma is part of the **carpel**, which includes the stigma, style, and ovary. Together, these structures form the female reproductive organ in flowers.
 
• Pollination—the transfer of pollen grains from the male anther to the female stigma—can occur through various agents, such as wind, water, insects, or animals.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Parts of a Flower:**
 
 
• **Stigma:** The receptive tip of the carpel where pollen grains land during pollination.
 
• **Style:** A tube-like structure that connects the stigma to the ovary, allowing the pollen tube to grow towards the ovule.
 
• **Ovary:** The part of the carpel that contains ovules, which develop into seeds after fertilization.
 
• **Filament:** The stalk that supports the anther, part of the male reproductive structure.
 
• **Petals:** Brightly colored structures that attract pollinators to the flower.
 
• **Sepals:** The outermost parts of a flower that protect the developing bud.
 
 
 
• **Pollination Process:**
 
 
• **Self-pollination:** Pollen from the same flower or plant lands on its stigma.
 
• **Cross-pollination:** Pollen from one flower is transferred to the stigma of another flower, promoting genetic diversity.
 
• **Agents of Pollination:** Wind, water, insects (like bees and butterflies), and animals help transfer pollen grains.
 
 
 
• **Fertilization:**
 
 
• Once the pollen tube reaches the ovary, it releases **male gametes**, which fuse with the **female gamete** (egg cell) inside the ovule to form a zygote.
 
• After fertilization, the ovule develops into a **seed**, and the ovary matures into a **fruit**.
 
 
 
• **Functions of Flower Parts:**
 
 
• **Stigma:** Captures pollen grains for fertilization.
 
• **Filament:** Positions the anther for effective pollen dispersal.
 
• **Petals:** Attract pollinators through color and scent.
 
• **Sepals:** Protect the flower during its bud stage.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

• **Option 2 (Stigma):** Correct, as it is the part where pollen grains land and germinate for fertilization to occur.
 
• **Option 3 (Petal):** Incorrect, as petals primarily serve to attract pollinators and do not directly participate in fertilization.
 
• **Option 4 (Sepal):** Incorrect, as sepals protect the flower bud and do not play a role in the fertilization process.

questions.question: Asexual reproduction is different from sexual reproduction. Which of the following options does not represent asexual reproduction?

options.text: Involvement of both male and female reproductive organs

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Involvement of both male and female reproductive organs**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Asexual reproduction** involves a single parent and does not require the participation of both male and female reproductive organs. Hence, the involvement of both male and female reproductive organs__ does not represent asexual reproduction. This is because asexual reproduction does not involve gametes or sexual organs.
 
• **Fission** is a type of asexual reproduction where an organism splits into two or more daughter cells, each of which becomes an independent organism. Examples include amoeba and bacteria. This process does not require male and female reproductive organs.
 
• **Regeneration** is another mode of asexual reproduction where organisms regrow lost or damaged parts, and in some cases, these parts develop into a new organism. For example, planarians and starfish exhibit regeneration. Male and female reproductive organs are not involved in this process.
 
• **Binary fission** is a specific type of fission where an organism divides into two equal parts. This is commonly seen in unicellular organisms like bacteria and protozoa. Again, this process does not involve male and female reproductive organs.
 
• Asexual reproduction is fundamentally different from sexual reproduction, as it does not require the fusion of male and female gametes. Instead, it involves a single organism replicating itself.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Key characteristics of asexual reproduction:**

 
 
• It involves only one parent, and the offspring are genetically identical to the parent.
 
• It occurs in both unicellular and multicellular organisms, such as bacteria, algae, fungi, and certain plants and animals.
 
• Common methods of asexual reproduction include binary fission, budding, fragmentation, regeneration, and vegetative propagation.
 
 
 
• **Types of asexual reproduction:**
 
 
• **Binary fission:** Common in prokaryotic organisms like bacteria. The parent cell splits into two identical daughter cells.
 
• **Budding:** Seen in organisms like yeast and hydra. A new organism grows as a small bud on the parent organism and eventually detaches.
 
• **Fragmentation:** Found in organisms like spirogyra and flatworms. The body of the organism breaks into fragments, each developing into a new organism.
 
• **Vegetative propagation:** Common in plants, where parts like stems, roots, or leaves give rise to new plants. Examples include potato tubers and bryophyllum leaves.
 
 
 
• **Comparison with sexual reproduction:**
 
 
• Sexual reproduction requires the involvement of two parents, with male and female gametes fusing to form a zygote.
 
• Offspring produced sexually show genetic variation, unlike asexual reproduction where offspring are clones of the parent.
 
• Sexual reproduction involves complex reproductive organs and processes, whereas asexual reproduction is simpler and faster.
 
 
 
• **Examples of organisms showing asexual reproduction:**
 
 
• **Binary fission:** Amoeba, Paramecium, and Euglena.
 
• **Budding:** Hydra and yeast.
 
• **Regeneration:** Starfish and planarians.
 
• **Vegetative propagation:** Potato, ginger, and onion.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Advantages of asexual reproduction:**

 
 
• It is a quick and efficient mode of reproduction, especially in stable environments.
 
• It does not require a mate, which is advantageous in isolated conditions.
 
 
 
• **Disadvantages of asexual reproduction:**
 
 
• Lack of genetic variation can make organisms vulnerable to environmental changes.
 
• It may lead to the accumulation of harmful mutations over generations.

questions.question: Which of the following describes the nature of the average speed?

options.text: It is a scalar quantity (only magnitude).
It is always equal to or less than the average velocity.
It is a vector quantity (magnitude and direction).

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**It is a scalar quantity (only magnitude).**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Average speed** is defined as the total distance traveled divided by the total time taken. It describes how fast an object moves irrespective of the direction.
 
• Since **average speed** considers only the magnitude (distance and time), it is classified as a **scalar quantity**. It does not incorporate direction.
 
• Average speed **cannot be negative** because distance traveled and time are always positive values. Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.
 
• Average speed is **greater than or equal to the magnitude of average velocity**. This is because average velocity depends on displacement, while average speed depends on distance. Statement 3 is incorrect.
 
• Average speed is not a **vector quantity** since it lacks direction. Statement 4 is incorrect.
 
• **Key formula**: Average speed = Total distance traveled / Total time taken.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Difference Between Average Speed and Average Velocity:**
 
 
• **Average speed** measures the total distance traveled per unit time, while **average velocity** measures displacement per unit time.
 
• **Average velocity** is a vector quantity, meaning it has both magnitude and direction, while **average speed** is scalar and only has magnitude.
 
 
 
• **Scalar vs. Vector Quantities:**
 
 
• **Scalar quantities** have only magnitude, e.g., distance, speed, mass, and time.
 
• **Vector quantities** have both magnitude and direction, e.g., velocity, displacement, force, and acceleration.
 
 
 
• **Applications of Average Speed:**
 
 
• Used in transportation to calculate travel times between locations.
 
• Helps determine efficiency in movement-related systems such as logistics and delivery services.
 
 
 
• **Real-Life Example:**
 
 
• If a car travels 100 km in 2 hours, its average speed is 100 km / 2 hours = 50 km/h.
 
• If the car returns to the starting point, average speed remains the same, but average velocity is zero due to zero displacement.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Formula Clarification:**
 
 
• Distance is the total length of the path traveled by an object.
 
• Displacement is the shortest straight-line distance between initial and final positions.
 
 
 
• **Key Physics Concept:**
 
 
• While average speed uses distance, average velocity uses displacement.
 
• In circular motion, average speed is non-zero, but average velocity can be zero if the object returns to its starting position.

questions.question: Which of the following phenomena is responsible for the blue colour of a clear sky?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Scattering**__.
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**
 
__ 
 
• The blue color of a clear sky is due to the phenomenon of **scattering of light**. When sunlight enters Earth's atmosphere, it interacts with air molecules and tiny particles. 
 
• **Rayleigh scattering** is the primary mechanism responsible for this phenomenon. It occurs when light is scattered by particles that are much smaller than the wavelength of the light, such as molecules of nitrogen and oxygen in the air. 
 
• Among the various colors of visible light, **blue light** has a shorter wavelength (around 450 nm) and higher energy compared to other colors like red, which has a longer wavelength (around 700 nm). Shorter wavelengths are scattered more efficiently by atmospheric particles. 
 
• As a result, the blue light is scattered in all directions, making the sky appear blue to an observer on the ground. 
 
• Other phenomena such as **reflection, dispersion, and refraction** are not primarily responsible for the blue color of the sky. They play roles in other optical phenomena but not in the coloring of the sky. 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**
 
__ 
 
• **Reflection:** 
 
• **Reflection** is the bouncing back of light when it hits a surface. It is responsible for phenomena like seeing images in mirrors and the shininess of surfaces like water or glass. 
 
• However, reflection does not explain the blue color of the sky. It mostly deals with light interaction at surfaces rather than with atmospheric particles. 
 
 
 
• **Dispersion:** 
 
• **Dispersion** is the splitting of light into its constituent colors, as seen in a rainbow. This happens when light passes through a prism or water droplets, which refract different wavelengths at different angles. 
 
• While dispersion is a fascinating phenomenon, it does not explain why the sky is blue, as the splitting of colors happens in more specific conditions. 
 
 
 
• **Scattering:** 
 
• **Rayleigh scattering** is specifically responsible for the blue sky. It occurs predominantly for shorter wavelengths like blue and violet. 
 
• Although violet light is scattered more than blue, our eyes are more sensitive to blue light, and much of the violet light is absorbed by the upper atmosphere, leaving the sky blue to our perception. 
 
 
 
• **Refraction:** 
 
• **Refraction** is the bending of light as it passes from one medium to another, such as from air to water. This is the principle behind lenses and effects like a straw appearing bent in a glass of water. 
 
• Refraction, while important in optics, does not contribute to the blue color of the sky. 
 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**
 
 
 
• **Red sunsets:** At sunrise and sunset, the sun appears red because sunlight has to travel a longer path through the atmosphere. Most of the shorter wavelengths (blue and violet) are scattered out, leaving primarily the longer wavelengths (red and orange). 
 
• **Other colors of the sky:** In pollution-free areas with minimal atmospheric particles, the sky can appear deeper blue due to less scattering of other colors. 
 
• **Moonlit sky:** During the night, the sky can appear black or grayish because there is insufficient sunlight for Rayleigh scattering to occur. 
 
• **Artificial scattering:** Experiments with scattering can be conducted using colloids and beam light to observe the Tyndall effect, which is analogous to Rayleigh scattering in the atmosphere.

questions.question: Which part of the brain controls involuntary actions such as blood pressure, salivation, and vomiting?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Medulla oblongata**__.
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**
 
__ 
 
• The **medulla oblongata** is the part of the brainstem located between the pons and the spinal cord. 
 
• It controls several **vital involuntary functions** such as **blood pressure regulation, heart rate, salivation, and vomiting**. 
 
• The medulla oblongata contains centers like the **cardiac center** (regulates heart rate), **vasomotor center** (controls blood vessel diameter), and the **respiratory center** (regulates breathing). 
 
• It is also involved in reflex actions, such as **coughing, sneezing, and swallowing**, which are critical for survival. 
 
• The medulla oblongata acts as a relay center, transmitting signals between the spinal cord and higher brain regions like the cerebrum and cerebellum. 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**
 
__ 
 
• **Cerebellum:** 
 
 
• The cerebellum is located at the back of the brain, below the cerebrum. 
 
• It primarily coordinates **voluntary movements**, balance, and posture. 
 
• It does not control involuntary actions like blood pressure or vomiting. *Hence, this option is incorrect.* 
 
 
 
• **Thalamus:** 
 
 
• The thalamus is a part of the forebrain that acts as a relay station for sensory signals traveling to the cerebrum. 
 
• It plays a role in regulating **consciousness, sleep, and alertness** but does not control involuntary functions. *Hence, this option is incorrect.* 
 
 
 
• **Cerebrum:** 
 
 
• The cerebrum is the largest part of the brain and is responsible for **higher brain functions** like thinking, memory, decision-making, and voluntary muscle movements. 
 
• It does not regulate involuntary actions like blood pressure or vomiting. *Hence, this option is incorrect.* 
 
 
 
• **Functions of the Medulla Oblongata:** 
 
 
• It ensures critical life-sustaining activities continue without conscious control, making it vital for survival. 
 
• It is part of the brainstem, which connects the brain to the spinal cord, facilitating communication between the central nervous system and the rest of the body. 
 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**
 
 
 
• Disruption or damage to the medulla oblongata can lead to severe consequences, including **respiratory failure** or **cardiovascular irregularities**. 
 
• The medulla also plays a role in reflexive responses to environmental stimuli, which are essential for protection and survival. 
 
• It is a critical area for drug interactions affecting the central nervous system, as many drugs impact the medulla’s control centers.

questions.question: Why is the filament of an electric bulb made of tungsten?

options.text: It has high resistance and can withstand high temperatures

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**It has high resistance and can withstand high temperatures**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The filament of an electric bulb is made of **tungsten** because it has a **high melting point** of approximately 3422°C, allowing it to withstand the extreme temperatures generated when electricity flows through it.
 
• Tungsten's **high resistance** ensures it generates sufficient heat to emit visible light when current passes through it, making it ideal for use in bulbs.
 
• Unlike metals with lower melting points, tungsten does not easily vaporize or melt under high temperatures, enhancing the bulb’s **longevity** and efficiency.
 
• Its **mechanical strength** at high temperatures prevents the filament from breaking easily, even when exposed to thermal stress during frequent on-off cycles of the bulb.
 
• Although tungsten is not the cheapest option, its unique properties make it indispensable for applications requiring durability and high-temperature performance. This is why it has been widely used in filament-based lighting for over a century.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Option 1 (It is cheaper):** Tungsten is not the cheapest material available. Other metals like aluminum or copper are cheaper but lack the necessary properties like high resistance and a high melting point. Hence, this option is incorrect__.
 
• **Option 2 (It is a good conductor):** Tungsten is a relatively good conductor of electricity but not the best. Metals like silver and copper are better conductors. However, tungsten’s suitability for filaments lies in its resistance and high melting point, not just conductivity. Hence, this option is __incorrect__.
 
• **Option 3 (It has high resistance and can withstand high temperatures):** Tungsten’s high resistance and ability to endure extreme heat make it the most suitable material for bulb filaments. These properties allow the filament to glow without melting, making this option __correct__.
 
• **Option 4 (Its melting point is low):** Tungsten has one of the highest melting points of any metal. A low melting point would cause the filament to melt quickly under high temperatures, which is not desirable. Hence, this option is __incorrect__.
 
• **History of Tungsten in Bulbs:** Tungsten filaments were introduced in the early 20th century, replacing earlier materials like carbon and tantalum. Their introduction revolutionized lighting by improving efficiency and durability.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **__Important Points__**

 
• **Why High Resistance is Important:** A material with high resistance converts electrical energy into heat efficiently, which is necessary for the filament to emit light.
 
• **Why High Melting Point is Critical:** Filaments operate at temperatures exceeding 2000°C. A high melting point prevents the filament from melting or vaporizing, ensuring durability.
 
• **Inert Gas in Bulbs:** To further prolong the filament's life, electric bulbs are filled with inert gases like argon or nitrogen to prevent oxidation and reduce evaporation of tungsten.
 
• **Applications of Tungsten:** Apart from light bulb filaments, tungsten is also used in X-ray tubes, high-temperature furnaces, and aerospace components due to its high melting point and strength.

questions.question: Anodising is typically performed on which metal?

The correct answer is __**Aluminium**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Anodising** is a process used primarily to increase the thickness of the natural oxide layer on the surface of **metals.**
 
• This process is most commonly applied to **aluminium** because aluminium naturally forms a thin oxide layer that can be thickened through anodising to enhance its properties.
 
• Anodising aluminium improves its **corrosion resistance**, wear resistance, and aesthetic appearance by allowing the addition of dyes and colors.
 
• The process involves immersing the aluminium in an **electrolytic solution** (usually sulfuric acid) and passing an electric current through it, resulting in the formation of an oxide layer.
 
• Other metals like **copper, zinc, and steel** are not typically anodised because their oxide layers are not as stable or protective as that of aluminium.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Uses of Anodised Aluminium:**

 
 
• Anodised aluminium is widely used in industries such as **aerospace, construction, and automotive** due to its enhanced durability and light weight.
 
• It is also used in **consumer products** like kitchen utensils, electronic casings, and decorative items for its aesthetic appeal.
 
• The oxide layer can be dyed in a variety of colors, making it suitable for decorative purposes.
 
 
 
• **Advantages of Anodising:**
 
 
• Enhances **corrosion resistance**, which is especially beneficial in harsh environments.
 
• Increases the **surface hardness** of aluminium, providing better wear resistance.
 
• Improves **adhesion** for paints and adhesives, making it versatile for different applications.
 
 
 
• **Why Aluminium is Preferred:**
 
 
• Aluminium naturally forms a **stable oxide layer**, which can be thickened and enhanced through the anodising process.
 
• It is **lightweight**, making it ideal for applications where weight is a factor.
 
• Other metals like copper and steel form oxide layers that are less stable or protective, making them unsuitable for anodising in most cases.
 
 
 
• **Process of Anodising:**
 
 
• The metal is cleaned to remove dirt, grease, or old oxide layers.
 
• The aluminium is then immersed in an **electrolyte bath**, such as sulfuric acid.
 
• An electric current is passed through the solution, causing **oxygen ions** to combine with the metal surface, forming an oxide layer.
 
• This oxide layer can be dyed or sealed to enhance its properties.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Copper:**

 
 
• Copper forms a greenish layer of **copper carbonate** (patina) when exposed to air, which is not suitable for anodising.
 
 
 
• **Zinc:**
 
 
• Zinc forms a white oxide layer that is not as protective or durable as the anodised layer on aluminium.
 
 
 
• **Steel:**
 
 
• Steel forms rust (iron oxide) when exposed to air and moisture, which is not conducive to anodising.
 
 
 
• **Applications of Aluminium:**
 
 
• Widely used in **aerospace, transportation, packaging, and construction** industries due to its properties.
 
• Its ability to be anodised further expands its applications in decorative and functional products.

questions.question:
Which of the following statements is/are true about villi in the small intestine?

**Statements:**

A: Increase surface area for absorption

B: Contain blood vessels

C: Help in excretion

D: Absorb digested nutrients

options.text: Only Statements A, B, and D
Only Statements A, B and C

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Only Statements A, B, and D**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Statement A: Increase surface area for absorption**

 
 
• The primary function of villi in the small intestine is to **increase the surface area** for absorption of nutrients.
 
• They are finger-like projections that greatly enhance the efficiency of nutrient absorption by providing a larger surface area.
 
• **Hence, this statement is correct.**
 
 
 
• **Statement B: Contain blood vessels**
 
 
• Each villus is richly supplied with **blood vessels** and lymphatic vessels, known as lacteals.
 
• These vessels help in the transport of absorbed nutrients, such as glucose and amino acids, into the bloodstream, while fats are absorbed into the lacteals.
 
• **Hence, this statement is correct.**
 
 
 
• **Statement C: Help in excretion**
 
 
• The villi are not involved in the process of excretion. They play no role in removing waste materials from the body.
 
• Their primary role is nutrient absorption, not waste elimination.
 
• **Hence, this statement is incorrect.**
 
 
 
• **Statement D: Absorb digested nutrients**
 
 
• The villi absorb digested nutrients such as carbohydrates, proteins, and fats. These are transported into the bloodstream or lymphatic system for distribution to the rest of the body.
 
• This function is vital for providing energy and building blocks for the body.
 
• **Hence, this statement is correct.**
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Structure of Villi**:

 
 
• Each villus is covered with a layer of columnar epithelial cells that have microvilli, further increasing the surface area for absorption.
 
• The core of the villus contains blood capillaries and a lymphatic vessel called a lacteal.
 
• Goblet cells present in the villi secrete mucus, aiding in the smooth movement of chyme.
 
 
 
• **Functions of the Small Intestine**:
 
 
• The small intestine is the main site of **digestion** and **absorption** of nutrients.
 
• It is divided into three parts: duodenum, jejunum, and ileum, each playing specific roles in digestion and absorption.
 
• Enzymes from the pancreas and bile from the liver aid in breaking down food into absorbable molecules.
 
 
 
• **Role of Lacteals**:
 
 
• Lacteals, the lymphatic vessels in the villi, are specifically responsible for the absorption of dietary fats.
 
• Fats are absorbed in the form of chylomicrons and transported through the lymphatic system into the bloodstream.
 
 
 
• **Diseases Affecting Villi**:
 
 
• Conditions like **celiac disease** damage the villi, leading to reduced nutrient absorption and malnutrition.
 
• Infections or inflammation in the intestine can also impair villi function.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Microvilli**: The epithelial cells of the villi have microvilli on their surface, forming a brush border that further enhances nutrient absorption.
 
• **Surface Area**: The combined effect of villi and microvilli increases the surface area of the small intestine by approximately 600 times.
 
• **Nutrient Transport**: Nutrients absorbed by the villi include glucose, amino acids, fatty acids, vitamins, and minerals.
 
• **Significance**: Proper functioning of villi is essential for maintaining good health, as they are crucial for nutrient uptake and energy supply.

questions.question: Which activity shows that particles of matter are continuously moving?

options.text: Fragrance of perfumes spreading in a room
Sugar settling at the bottom of a glass of water
Water being heated to its boiling point

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Fragrance of perfumes spreading in a room**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Diffusion in Gases:** The spreading of perfume fragrance in a room is an example of **diffusion**, which occurs due to the continuous movement of particles in gases. Particles of the perfume mix with air particles and spread throughout the room.
 
• **Particle Kinetic Energy:** The motion of particles in gases is due to their **kinetic energy**. Gas particles move randomly and continuously, colliding with one another and with surfaces, causing the fragrance to spread.
 
• **Observation of Matter's Behavior:** This activity demonstrates that **particles of matter are in constant motion**. The ability of the perfume molecules to travel across the room is evidence of this continuous movement.
 
• **State of Matter:** In gases, particles have the most freedom of movement compared to solids and liquids. This explains why the fragrance spreads quickly and uniformly in a room.
 
• **Real-life Example:** The concept of diffusion is used to explain various phenomena in daily life, such as the spread of smoke or the smell of food cooking in the kitchen.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Explanation of Other Options:**

 
 
• **Ice melting at room temperature:** This involves a change in the state of matter from solid to liquid. While it indicates that particles gain energy and move faster, it does not demonstrate the continuous movement of particles within matter as clearly as diffusion.
 
• **Sugar settling at the bottom of a glass of water:** When sugar settles, it does not show the movement of particles actively. However, if sugar dissolves, it demonstrates diffusion, which involves particle motion.
 
• **Water being heated to its boiling point:** Heating water increases the kinetic energy of the particles, leading to a phase change (liquid to gas). While this shows particle movement, it is not as evident as the diffusion of perfume fragrance in the air.
 
 
 
• **Diffusion in Different States of Matter:**
 
 
• Diffusion occurs in **solids, liquids, and gases**, but it is fastest in gases due to the larger spaces between particles and their higher kinetic energy.
 
• In liquids, diffusion is slower compared to gases because particles are closer and experience more resistance.
 
• In solids, diffusion is extremely slow as particles are tightly packed and can only vibrate in place.
 
 
 
• **Applications of Diffusion:**
 
 
• In biology, diffusion explains how oxygen and carbon dioxide are exchanged in the lungs during respiration.
 
• In chemistry, diffusion is used to mix substances without stirring, such as in chemical reactions or preparation of solutions.
 
• In everyday life, diffusion is observed in air fresheners spreading their fragrance in a room.
 
 
 
• **Factors Affecting Diffusion:**
 
 
• **Temperature:** Higher temperatures increase particle kinetic energy, speeding up diffusion.
 
• **Medium:** Diffusion is fastest in gases, slower in liquids, and slowest in solids.
 
• **Particle Size:** Smaller particles diffuse faster than larger ones.
 
• **Concentration Gradient:** A higher concentration difference between two regions increases the rate of diffusion.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Brownian Motion:** The random movement of particles suspended in a fluid (liquid or gas) due to collisions with the molecules of the surrounding medium is known as **Brownian motion**. This phenomenon further supports the idea that particles of matter are in continuous motion.
 
• **Real-Life Example of Brownian Motion:** The zigzag movement of pollen grains on the surface of water demonstrates this concept.
 
• **Historical Context:** The concept of diffusion and Brownian motion was studied by **Albert Einstein** in 1905, which provided significant evidence for the existence and movement of atoms and molecules.
 
• **Practical Implications:** Understanding diffusion helps in developing technologies like air purifiers, chemical reactors, and efficient drug delivery systems in medicine.

questions.question:
A shopkeeper announces the following three discount schemes. Which scheme is the most beneficial for the customer?

A. Buy 5 items and get 2 identical items free

B. Two successive discounts of 13% and 38%

C. Two equal successive discounts of 21%
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Scheme A: Buy 5 get 22 free ⇒ pay for 5, get 27 ⇒ effective discount = (22/27) × 100 ≈ 81.48%

Scheme B: 13% and 38% successive ⇒ net = 1 − (0.87 × 0.62) = 46.06%

Scheme C: 21% twice ⇒ net = 1 − (0.79 × 0.79) = 37.59%

Compare: 81.48% > 46.06% > 37.59%

**∴ Answer = Scheme A is most beneficial**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Three discount schemes A, B, C

**Formula used:**

Successive discount = 1 − (product of remaining fractions)

**Calculation:**

⇒ Scheme A: Buy 5 get 22 free

⇒ Total items = 5 + 22 = 27

⇒ Effective discount = (22 ÷ 27) × 100 ≈ 81.48%

⇒ Scheme B: 13% and 38%

⇒ Net discount = 1 − (0.87 × 0.62) = 1 − 0.5394 = 46.06%

⇒ Scheme C: 21% and 21%

⇒ Net discount = 1 − (0.79 × 0.79) = 1 − 0.6241 = 37.59%

⇒ Comparing all: Scheme A gives highest discount

**∴ The correct answer is Scheme A.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Successive Discount

Net discount = 1 − (1 − d1)(1 − d2)

Free Item Concept

Effective discount = Free items ÷ Total items × 100

Comparison Trick

Convert all schemes into percentage discount

Key Insight

Higher effective discount ⇒ better scheme

questions.question: A metallic sphere of radius 36 cm is dropped into a cylindrical vessel, which is partly filled with water. The diameter of the vessel is 4.8 metres. If the sphere is completely submerged, find by how much the surface of the water will rise.

The measure of an exterior angle of a triangle is exactly equal to the sum of the measures of its two opposite (remote) interior angles. Using this theorem skips the need to find the third interior angle.

A : B = 4 : 5 and B : C = 4 : 5 ⇒ A : B : C = 16 : 20 : 25

C : D = 6 : 7 ⇒ match C = 150 ⇒ multiply by 6

A : B : C : D = 96 : 120 : 150 : 175

Total parts = 541 ⇒ 1 part = 3787 ÷ 541 = 7

**∴ A = 96 × 7 = 672**

Combine ratios by equalizing common terms

⇒ A : B = 4 : 5 and B : C = 4 : 5

⇒ Make B equal ⇒ LCM of 5 and 4 = 20

⇒ A : B = 16 : 20 and B : C = 20 : 25

⇒ So A : B : C = 16 : 20 : 25

⇒ Now C : D = 6 : 7

⇒ Make C equal ⇒ LCM of 25 and 6 = 150

⇒ Multiply first ratio by 6 ⇒ 96 : 120 : 150

⇒ Multiply second ratio by 25 ⇒ 150 : 175

⇒ Final ratio = 96 : 120 : 150 : 175

⇒ Total parts = 96 + 120 + 150 + 175 = 541

⇒ Value of 1 part = 3787 ÷ 541 = 7

⇒ A = 96 × 7 = 672

**∴ The correct answer is 672.**

Three of the following four are alike in a certain way based on the given arrangement and so form a group. Which is the one that does not belong to that group?
questions.solution:
**Given:** Six persons, A, B, C, D, E and F, are sitting in a row, facing north.

1. A sits immediate right of E.

2. B sits fourth to the left of E.

3. Only one person sits between B and F.

4. C sits immediate left of F.

5, D sits second to the left of A.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/8ab5b06ff0ff680f57bc25d9f9a74c07b20c741ca3bdfc447ae2b50454fdb291.png] 

Let's check each option:

1. DE → D is to the immediate left of E.

2. FD → F is is to the immediate left of D.

3. CF → C is to the immediate left of F.

4. BA → B and A re sitting at extreme ends of the row.

All options except BA are alike in a certain way and form a group. 

Thus, BA is the odd one out. 

Hence, the correct answer is "Option 4".

questions.question: The Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA) has notified new rules for the cancellation of the registration of Overseas Citizens of India in August 2025. Under which Act have these rules been issued?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Citizenship Act, 1955**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA)** notified the new rules in **August 2025** to streamline the process of **registration** and **cancellation** of the **Overseas Citizen of India (OCI)** status.
 
• These rules were issued under the **Citizenship Act, 1955**, which is the primary legislation governing the acquisition, determination, and termination of **Indian citizenship** and **OCI** status.
 
• Under **Section 7D** of the **Citizenship Act, 1955**, the **Central Government** holds the authority to cancel the **OCI registration** if the person has shown disaffection towards the **Constitution of India** or violated any laws notified by the government.
 
• The **2025 notification** emphasizes that any **OCI cardholder** found involved in activities prejudicial to the **sovereignty, integrity, and security** of **India** will face immediate **cancellation** of their status.
 
• The **OCI card** is a multipurpose document that allows foreign citizens of Indian origin to live and work in **India** indefinitely, but it does not confer **voting rights** or the right to hold **public office**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Citizenship Act, 1955:**

 
 
• This **Act** provides for the acquisition of citizenship by **birth, descent, registration, naturalization**, and **incorporation of territory**.
 
• It has been amended several times, most notably in **1986, 1992, 2003, 2005, 2015, and 2019**.
 
• The **OCI scheme** was introduced by the **Citizenship (Amendment) Act, 2005** in response to demands for dual citizenship by the **Indian diaspora**.
 
 
 
• **Passport Act, 1967:**
 
 
• This **Act** regulates the issuance of **passports** and travel documents to **Indian citizens**.
 
• While it governs travel, it does not deal with the **registration** or **cancellation** of **OCI** status. ***Hence, option 1 is incorrect.***
 
 
 
• **Foreigners Act, 1946:**
 
 
• This **Act** empowers the **Indian government** to regulate the **entry, stay, and departure** of **foreign nationals** in **India**.
 
• Although **OCI holders** are foreign nationals, their specific **registration** rights are governed by the **Citizenship Act** rather than this general act. ***Hence, option 2 is incorrect.***
 
 
 
• **Indian Penal Code, 1860:**
 
 
• This was the official **criminal code** of **India** (now replaced by **Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita** in recent reforms).
 
• It defines **offenses** and provides **punishments** but does not contain provisions for **citizenship** or **OCI registration**. ***Hence, option 3 is incorrect.***
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Rights of OCI Cardholders:**
 
• They enjoy **parity with Non-Resident Indians (NRIs)** in economic, financial, and educational fields, except in the acquisition of **agricultural or plantation properties**.
 
• **Grounds for Cancellation:**
 
• Registration can be cancelled if it was obtained through **fraud**, false representation, or if the **OCI holder** is sentenced to **imprisonment** for not less than **two years** within **five years** of registration.
 
• **The 2019 Amendment:**
 
• The **Citizenship (Amendment) Act, 2019** significantly expanded the **Central Government's** power to cancel **OCI status** if the holder violates any **local law** as specified by the **MHA**.
 
• **Designation:** The **Ministry of Home Affairs** is the nodal ministry for all matters relating to **citizenship** and **foreigners' registration** in **India**.

questions.question: In July 2025, the Defence Research and Development Organisation successfully conducted flight tests of the Unmanned Aerial Vehicle Launched Precision Guided Missile (ULPGM)-V3 at the National Open Area Range test facility in ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kurnool, Andhra Pradesh**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In **July 2025**, the **Defence Research and Development Organisation (DRDO)** successfully conducted the flight tests of the **Unmanned Launch Precision Guided Missile (ULPGM)-V3**.
 
• The testing took place at the **National Open Area Range (NOAR)**, which is located in **Kurnool, Andhra Pradesh**.
 
• The **ULPGM-V3** is a sophisticated air-to-surface missile specifically designed to be launched from **Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs)** to engage ground targets with high accuracy.
 
• During the flight tests, the missile's **precision guidance system**, **aerodynamic stability**, and **warhead triggering mechanism** were evaluated under realistic combat scenarios.
 
• This successful trial represents a significant step toward indigenous **precision-strike capabilities** and reduces dependency on foreign weapon systems for India's growing drone fleet.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **DRDO (Defence Research and Development Organisation):**

 
 
• It was established in **1958** and functions under the **Ministry of Defence**, Government of India.
 
• Headquartered in **New Delhi**, its primary mission is to achieve self-reliance in critical defense technologies and systems.
 
• It operates a network of more than **50 laboratories** across the country developing various technologies like aeronautics, armaments, electronics, and missiles.
 
 
 
• **National Open Area Range (NOAR), Kurnool:**
 
 
• Located in the **Orvakal** region of **Kurnool district**, this facility provides a vast, unobstructed area for testing various missile and rocket systems.
 
• It complements other major testing sites like the **Integrated Test Range (ITR)** at **Chandipur, Odisha**.
 
• The **Andhra Pradesh** government has been actively supporting the development of defense corridors and specialized testing ranges within the state.
 
 
 
• **Unmanned Launch Precision Guided Missiles (ULPGM):**
 
 
• These are "smart" munitions that utilize **laser guidance**, **GPS**, or **Inertial Navigation Systems (INS)** to strike targets with minimal collateral damage.
 
• The integration of such missiles with indigenous UAVs like the **TAPAS-BH-201** or **Archer** enhances the tactical offensive reach of the **Indian Armed Forces**.
 
• The **V3 variant** indicates an advanced iteration with improved range, seeker technology, and weight-to-payload ratio.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Strategic Significance:** The development of the **ULPGM-V3** aligns with the **Atmanirbhar Bharat** (Self-Reliant India) initiative in the defense sector.
 
• **Recent Trends:** Modern warfare is increasingly shifting toward **Unmanned Combat Aerial Vehicles (UCAVs)**, making specialized miniature precision munitions a critical requirement for **21st-century** defense strategy.
 
• **Geographic Location:** **Kurnool** is strategically chosen for its topography and lower population density, ensuring safety during high-velocity **missile flight trials**.

questions.question: The Parliament of India passed the Immigration and Foreigners Bill in April ________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**2025**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Indian Parliament** successfully passed the **Immigration and Foreign Subjects Bill** in **April 2025** to modernize the nation's legal framework regarding international travel and residency.
 
• The primary objective of this bill is to consolidate and replace aging statutes, such as the **Foreigners Act, 1946**, ensuring that the regulation of **foreign nationals** aligns with contemporary **national security** requirements.
 
• The **2025** legislation introduces a comprehensive **digital tracking system** for all foreign subjects, requiring mandatory **biometric registration** for those staying in the **country** for more than **90 days**.
 
• It grants the **Central Government** enhanced powers to regulate the **entry, stay, and departure** of individuals, specifically targeting the prevention of **illegal immigration** and **visa overstays**.
 
• The bill also simplifies the process for **skilled professionals** and **investors**, aiming to boost the **Indian economy** by attracting global talent through a more transparent **visa regime**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **The Foreigners Act, 1946:**

 
 
• This was the foundational law used by the **Government of India** for decades to regulate the presence of foreigners. It gave the **Executive** broad discretionary powers to detain and **deport** individuals deemed to be in the **country** illegally.
 
 
 
• **Bureau of Immigration (BoI):**
 
 
• The **BoI** is the dedicated agency responsible for managing **Immigration Check Posts (ICPs)** at **airports**, **seaports**, and **land borders**. It functions under the **Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA)**.
 
 
 
• **e-Visa Facility:**
 
 
• India provides **e-Visas** to citizens of over **160 countries**. The new legislative changes in **2025** aim to further digitize this process, reducing the **processing time** for **Tourist**, **Business**, and **Medical visas**.
 
 
 
• **Passport (Entry into India) Act, 1920:**
 
 
• This act requires persons entering **India** to possess valid **passports**. The **Immigration and Foreign Subjects Bill, 2025** works in tandem with this act to ensure **border integrity**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **National Security:** The **2025 bill** emphasizes the use of **Artificial Intelligence (AI)** to flag suspicious **travel patterns**, thereby assisting **intelligence agencies** in maintaining internal safety.
 
• **Visa Categories:** The **legislation** clarifies the rights and restrictions associated with various categories, such as **Employment Visas**, **Student Visas**, and **Research Visas**, ensuring that **foreign subjects** comply with the specific purposes of their visit.
